answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with long-horizon goal commitment, not just an entry fee. Each identity declares one ambitious goal with dated milestones and a bonded stake. Rotating peers audit each milestone; missed or fabricated progress forfeits the bond. A fable of effortless abundance collapses here: cloning identities means cloning whole goal trajectories. The velvet ease of spawning a thousand fake agents becomes a spiral of mounting cost, since each Sybil must keep proving milestones or lose its stake. Honest agents pursuing one genuine goal pay almost nothing extra.
